Esto es lo más destacado de España en las noticias recientes (hasta el 18 de octubre de 2026):

**Política: elecciones generales el 29 de noviembre**
- Tras el adelanto electoral convocado a principios de octubre, la atención se centra ya en la precampaña. Según EFE, las coaliciones que concurren a los comicios están definidas, y aún faltan por conocerse los cabezas de lista provinciales de formaciones como el PP y Vox (Temas del día de EFE España del domingo 18 de octubre de 2026).
- En la izquierda hay tensiones: Rufián reconoce su fracaso al intentar la unidad, y Belarra pide a IU que revise su negativa a pactar con Podemos en los territorios (Temas del día de EFE España del viernes 16 de octubre de 2026).
- La Junta Electoral Central declaró que no puede intervenir en el voto por correo sin indicios de irregularidades (mismo resumen de EFE).

**Protestas por la vivienda**
- El 5 de octubre, una manifestación en Barcelona reunió a 120.000 personas según los organizadores, y terminó con cargas policiales y contenedores quemados (Así te hemos contado la actualidad política el 5 de octubre de 2026).

**Ceuta y el Rey**
- El Rey rechazó que la llegada de migrantes a Ceuta sea un problema migratorio, calificándola de "otra cosa y de otra dimensión" (Libertad Digital, noticias del 13 de octubre). Durante el desfile del 12 de octubre hubo abucheos e insultos contra Pedro Sánchez (elDiario.es, resumen del 12 de octubre).

**Meteorología**
- La DANA Adam dejó más de 100 incidencias en El Ejido y activó la alerta roja en zonas de Almería, Valencia, Alicante y Barcelona (Temas del día de EFE, domingo 18 de octubre).

**Economía y justicia**
- El alquiler sigue tensionado por la falta de oferta, según una entrevista de EFE con la economista Paloma Taltavull (EFE, 18 de octubre).
- En el caso Plus Ultra, el prestamista niega haber blanqueado dinero del rescate del Gobierno (Temas del día de EFE, 16 de octubre).

**Deportes**
- El Real Madrid pidió la dimisión de Javier Tebas por sus declaraciones sobre la comunicación del club, en plena polémica en LaLiga (Temas del día de EFE, 16 de octubre).

Si quieres, puedo buscar más detalle sobre alguno de estos temas, como la campaña electoral o la alerta por la DANA.

Here are the main Spanish stories from the past week, mostly dated October 12–16, 2026.

**Politics**
- Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has called a snap general election for 29 November. The move followed Congress rejecting two housing decrees from his government. Congress voted down the measures on Friday, despite last-minute negotiations to secure enough support.
- The government's housing decree is already having effects. One report says landlords pulled 4,235 homes from the rental market in just 10 days.

**Migration and Ceuta**
- King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia made their first visit to Ceuta since 2007. They received a warm welcome on Tuesday, 13 October. The trip came after a summer migration crisis there.
- Spain and Italy agreed to end border checks after a dispute linked to the Ceuta crisis, according to Olive Press headlines from 16 October.
- A Spanish NGO has halted Mediterranean rescue operations, citing fuel prices, according to Al Jazeera.

**Protests and National Day**
- Spain's National Day on 12 October was marked by demonstrations in Barcelona in support of Spanish unity.
- In Madrid, police charged education protesters at a student picket line at Complutense University during a strike in defence of public education. Four protesters have been arrested, according to police sources.

**Transport**
- Train drivers have called a strike for Wednesday, October 29, with risk of cancellations and delays on Spain's rail network, including Cercanías commuter trains. The union, Semaf, says talks have stalled.
- Euro Weekly News also reports an ongoing indefinite strike by ground handling staff at Barcelona-El Prat Airport.

**Weather**
- Costa del Sol is bracing for torrential rain as AEMET issues yellow warnings ahead of a weekend deluge.
- Costa Blanca has an "unusual storm" threatening a sudden cold snap.

**Other news**
- Two residents died and four were critically hurt at a Málaga care home after a lift fell about 50 feet, according to The Olive Press.
- Football: Real Madrid's president criticised La Liga's president, Javier Tebas, after Tebas compared Real Madrid's TV channel to Nazi propaganda. Separately, FIFA punished Spain over Islamophobic chants during a friendly against Egypt.

These come from search snippets, not full articles, so details may be incomplete. Several sources were also listed with inconsistent dates. For the latest updates, check Euronews, The Local, or Al Jazeera's Spain pages directly.

content.text:
Here are the three most important stories in Spain from October 11–18, 2026:

1. **Election campaign:** Spain is heading into a snap general election on November 29, which Pedro Sánchez called on October 5 after Congress rejected his housing decrees. This week the coalitions were finalised and there was open infighting on the left: Rufián admitted his push for unity had failed, and Belarra urged IU to reconsider its refusal to run with Podemos. [EFE via Infobae, Oct 16](https://www.infobae.com/espana/agencias/2026/10/16/temas-del-dia-de-efe-espana-del-viernes-16-de-octubre-de-2026-1330-horas/)

2. **Royal visit to Ceuta:** On October 13, King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia made their first visit to Ceuta since 2007, after this summer's migration crisis there, and the King said the situation was "something else and of another dimension" rather than simply a migration problem. [The Local](https://www.thelocal.es/20261015/today-in-spain-a-roundup-of-the-latest-news-on-thursday-99) / [Libertad Digital](https://www.libertaddigital.com/espana/2026-10-13/)

3. **Storm Adam:** A DANA storm called Adam caused more than 100 emergency incidents in El Ejido and triggered red alerts in parts of Almería, Valencia, Alicante and Barcelona this weekend. [EFE via Infobae, Oct 18](https://www.infobae.com/espana/agencias/2026/10/17/temas-del-dia-de-efe-espana-del-domingo-18-de-octubre-de-2026/)

The ranking is my own judgment. Other stories this week included a reported loss of more than 4,000 rental listings after the housing decree, a rail strike called for October 29, and Real Madrid's feud with LaLiga president Javier Tebas. These summaries come from search results and news roundups, not full articles.
